question: Which book of the departure am I?
reference: Exodus 1-40 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Exodus, Book Of')

clues: I open with Israel enslaved in Egypt and a baby drawn out of the Nile.
I tell of ten plagues, a Passover lamb, and a sea that parted.
At a mountain, a nation received a law written on stone.
I close with a portable tent of worship filled with God's glory.

question: Which book of visions and a lions' den am I?
reference: Daniel 1-12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Daniel, Book Of')

clues: I follow a young captive who refused the king's rich food.
He interpreted dreams of a great metal image and a hand writing on a wall.
He was thrown to lions for praying, and came out unharmed.
My later chapters unfold prophecies of one world power after another.

question: Which book of wise sayings am I?
reference: Proverbs 1-31 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Proverbs, Book Of')

clues: I am largely a collection of short, pointed sayings for everyday living.
I picture wisdom as a woman calling out in the streets.
Much of me is credited to Solomon.
I close with a poem praising a capable wife.

question: Which Gospel that opens with a genealogy am I?
reference: Matthew 1-28 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Matthew, Good News According to')

clues: I begin by tracing Jesus' line from Abraham through David, in three sets of fourteen.
I record the visit of the astrologers and the flight to Egypt.
I gather Jesus' teaching into five long blocks, starting with the Sermon on the Mount.
I quote the Hebrew prophets again and again to show they were fulfilled.

question: Which letter comparing Christ to the old system am I?
reference: Hebrews 1-13 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Hebrews, Letter to the')

clues: I argue that the Son is greater than the angels, than Moses, and than the high priest Aaron.
I explain the tabernacle and the Day of Atonement as shadows of better things.
My eleventh chapter is a long roll call of people who acted in faith.
I urge readers not to shrink back, but to run the race with endurance.

question: Which sign in the sky am I?
reference: Genesis 9:12-17; Ezekiel 1:28; Revelation 4:3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Rainbow')

clues: God set me in the clouds after the floodwaters had gone down.
I am the token of a covenant with Noah and every living creature.
My meaning is that never again will a flood destroy all flesh.
Ezekiel and John both saw me encircling God's throne.

question: Which covenant sign am I?
reference: Genesis 17; Exodus 4:24-26; Acts 15 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Circumcision')

clues: God commanded me for Abraham and every male in his household, on the eighth day.
I was the physical mark of the covenant God made with him.
Moses nearly died on the road for neglecting me for his son.
Paul argued at length that I was not required of non-Jewish Christians.

question: Which sacrifice am I?
reference: Exodus 12; John 19:36; 1 Corinthians 5:7 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Passover')

clues: I had to be a year-old male without defect, chosen on the tenth day and killed on the fourteenth.
My blood was brushed on the doorframes so the destroyer would pass over.
Not one of my bones was to be broken.
Paul called Christ our version of me.

question: Which little vessel am I?
reference: Exodus 2:1-10 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Moses', p. 434)

clues: A mother wove me from papyrus and waterproofed me with tar and pitch.
She placed her three-month-old son in me and set me among the reeds of the Nile.
A princess came down to bathe, saw me, and had me brought to her.
The baby's own sister was watching, and arranged for his mother to nurse him.

question: Which pair of priests am I?
reference: Leviticus 10:1-7 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nadab No. 1')

clues: We were the two oldest sons of the first high priest.
On the day the tabernacle service began, we offered fire that God had not commanded.
Fire came out from before God and consumed us.
Our father was told not to mourn us publicly.

question: Which rebel against Moses am I?
reference: Numbers 16 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Korah No. 3')

clues: I was a Levite, a cousin of Moses and Aaron.
I gathered 250 chiefs and told Moses the whole assembly was holy.
Moses said God would show whom he had chosen.
The ground opened and swallowed me and my household, and fire consumed the 250.

question: Which brother-killing king am I?
reference: Judges 9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Abimelech No. 4')

clues: My father was the judge Gideon, and my mother was a servant woman from Shechem.
I hired reckless men and murdered seventy of my brothers on a single stone.
Only the youngest, Jotham, escaped, and he shouted a parable of the trees from a mountaintop.
I died when a woman dropped a millstone on my head, and I had my armor-bearer finish me off.

question: Which idol-maker of Ephraim am I?
reference: Judges 17-18 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Micah No. 3')

clues: I confessed to my mother that I had taken 1,100 pieces of silver from her.
She had part of it made into a carved image, which I set up in my house.
I hired a wandering Levite to be my personal priest.
Men of the tribe of Dan passed through, took my idols and my priest, and left me with nothing.

question: Which rival wife am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 1 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Peninnah')

clues: I shared a husband with a woman named Hannah.
I had children, and she had none.
Year after year I taunted and provoked her over it until she wept and could not eat.
In the end her prayer was answered, and her son became a great prophet.

question: Which spared enemy king am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 15 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Agag')

clues: I was king of the Amalekites.
King Saul defeated my people but kept me and the best of the livestock alive, against God's command.
That disobedience cost Saul the kingdom.
The prophet Samuel called for me and cut me to pieces before Jehovah at Gilgal.

question: Which town of Saul am I?
reference: Judges 19-20; 1 Samuel 10-11; Hosea 9:9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Gibeah No. 3')

clues: I was the hometown of Israel's first king, and he ruled from me.
A horrifying crime against a Levite's concubine here set off a civil war that nearly destroyed the tribe of Benjamin.
Prophets held me up as a byword for Israel's corruption.
I sat in the territory of Benjamin, just north of Jerusalem.
